title: The garden of forking paths

data.source: Sunspot cycle table (SILSO, Royal Observatory of Belgium, as typed into checks/es-sunspot.py); Hudson Bay lynx pelts 1821 to 1934 (R datasets); NGRIP oxygen-isotope record on the GICC05 timescale (NOAA). Each compared with 300 shuffles of itself. Adapted from colloquy/lab/epistemic/02_mapping_freedom.py.
data.licence: SILSO CC BY-NC 4.0; R datasets GPL-3; NOAA public archive. See each folder's SOURCE.txt.

prediction: The share of fair mappings that hold on the real sunspot record lies inside the middle 95 per cent of the shares seen in 300 shuffled worlds, and at least one fair mapping holds in more than half of the shuffled worlds. (A replication: written after the lens's own run had been read.)
baseline: The one mapping each room registered first, and the shuffled record, which has no carry-over by construction.
why: This book tests no line of CRR. It measures how much room the worker had. On the sunspot record 70 of 384 fair mappings pass the seed bet, a share of 0.182; on shuffled copies the share is 0.177, and in every one of 300 shuffled worlds at least one mapping passed. A fit that was searched for is not evidence. One written down first is worth a little.
claim_kind: none of CRR's: a book about method (how free the mapping is)

wall.columns: q (6) x first seed (2) x loss (2) x rivals (2)

second_check: re-run by a library worker who did not write the menus; not checked by a person
operating_characteristics: Not a test of CRR, so none are claimed.
